name: Park Avenue Apartments
headline: The Colorado Coalition for the Homeless is building 60 one-bedroom permanent supportive homes for people leaving homelessness (30% to 60% AMI) on the former La Quinta hotel site in Denver's Globeville neighborhood. It won 2025 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows how a COVID-era hotel shelter bought with city ARPA and state Operation Turnkey money can be turned into permanent supportive housing: 9% credits plus state vouchers on all 60 units, a city loan, Prop 123 money and a federal earmark. The deal financed in May 2026 and broke ground in July 2026, after two earlier tax credit bids had failed.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking 2026-07-22); lease-up expected 2027
status.detail: CCH says it closed financing on Friday 2026-05-15, and its general contractor started demolition on 2026-05-18. BusinessDen photographed the hotel being demolished on 2026-06-02. City officials and CCH held a groundbreaking on 2026-07-22, and the city and CCH expect lease-up to start in 2027. No public certificate of occupancy or completion date exists yet.

next_step: Watch Denver building permit and inspection records for 3721 N. Globeville Road, CCH lease-up notices in 2027, and a new council resolution for the $1.35M services agreement, which the city's file lists as tabled.

key_numbers.meaning: Permanent supportive housing for people exiting homelessness: 26 at 30% AMI, 20 at 40%, 7 at 50% and 7 at 60%. State project-based vouchers cover all 60.
About $16M over the 10-year credit period, plus $650,000 state credit and $78,000 TOC credit. CCH expected the credits to bring in more than $17M of private investment.
Denver Council adopted the HOST loan on 2026-04-20 (Resolution 26-0501, 720-month term). The State Housing Board approved $3.6M of Prop 123 funds in November 2025.
Financing closed 2026-05-15 and demolition began 2026-05-18. Lease-up is planned for 2027.

facts.value: 3721 N. Globeville Road, Denver 80216 (the city and CCH's 2026 records). CHFA and the earlier filings use 3500-3600 Park Avenue West, at Park Avenue W and Globeville Road by the I-25 interchange.
N, SH: new construction, supportive housing (code meanings inferred from the project description)
Four stories and 61,244 sq ft, Type V-A wood frame with glulam timber beams (the application describes 3 and 4 stories). Trauma-informed design by Davis Partnership Architects.
C-MX-8. Council rezoned it from I-B UO-2 by ordinance (Council Bill 22-1214), passed 2022-11-14. The applicant says the project is a use by right and needs no other public approvals.
2.24 acres. This 60-unit building is the first phase; CCH's long-term goal is up to 200 units on the site.
The applicant says the site is in a 2025 Qualified Census Tract
RTD Route 38 stops at Park Avenue and Globeville Road, and the 41st & Fox light rail station (B and G lines) is about half a mile away. Residents get RTD EcoPasses.
Colorado Division of Housing state project-based vouchers on all 60 units
The applicant says a partnership with Denver Housing Authority supports the property tax exemption

background.text: The site held the La Quinta hotel and the Old West Pancake House. CCH bought it in December 2021 with help from Denver HOST and state Operation Turnkey money, and used the 103-room hotel as non-congregate shelter during COVID and later as transitional housing.

On 2022-09-26 the City Council approved $5M in ARPA funds for the acquisition (Resolution 22-1097). The agreement carries a 60-year covenant and requires the shelter units to become supportive housing within four years.

The application says the shelter's grant-funded operations would expire in mid-2025 and that regulatory terms require the site to become affordable housing, so redevelopment money was needed to avoid default.
Council rezoned 3500 and 3600 Park Avenue West from industrial (I-B UO-2) to C-MX-8 by ordinance (Council Bill 22-1214), passed 2022-11-14. The committee had approved filing on 2022-10-04.

The same 60-unit project applied in 2024 Round One for 9% credits and was not funded. It then applied in 2024 Round Two for state and 4% credits. The 2025 application says it was not funded in earlier rounds but held Division of Housing Tier 1 status.

The project is in Denver's Affordable Housing Review Team process, and its concept site development plan has been reviewed. HUD issued an environmental release. A Phase II found arsenic and lead below cleanup levels, and a vapor barrier is planned because of past bulk fuel storage on the site.

Off-site work paid for by the project: a raised crosswalk and a pedestrian rapid flashing beacon at the free right turn onto I-25/I-70, plus a new curb, tree lawn and 8-foot detached sidewalk on Park Avenue.
The Park Avenue Inn shelter closed at the end of January 2026, and the site was empty and fenced by early February 2026.

On-site services from CCH staff include behavioral health, case management, addiction recovery, job readiness and financial literacy. The application says these are funded by Division of Housing tenancy support services, Medicaid, fundraising and cash flow.

discrepancies.text: CCH's May 2025 release says the Coalition bought the site in 2020, while the application narratives, CCH's 2026 releases and BusinessDen say December 2021 (the city says 2021).
BusinessDen puts the 2021 purchase price at $11 million, while Westword said around $12 million.
CHFA and the earlier filings give the address as 3500-3600 Park Avenue West, while the city's 2026 resolutions and CCH's 2026 releases use 3721 N. Globeville Road.
The 2025 application names FirstBank as the construction and permanent lender, while CCH's 2026 releases say Wells Fargo provides the construction financing and tax credit equity.
The application describes a building of 3 and 4 stories, while CCH and the city describe a four-story building.

open_questions: Total development cost and the amounts of the Wells Fargo construction loan, the tax credit equity, the permanent debt and the FHLB AHP award. Press reports cite a $34M budget and a $15.3M loan, but those articles could not be fetched or are paywalled, so the figures are not used here.
Whether the $1.35M HOST services agreement was re-filed under a new resolution, since Resolution 26-0502 is listed as tabled.
Length of the CHFA affordability period (LURA) for the new building.
Building permit number and issue date, and the planned completion month.
Timing and funding for later phases on the 2.24-acre site, given CCH's goal of up to 200 units there.
